title: Arrival watermarking harness to measure p95 under mixed-batch backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that instruments arrival 'watermarks' and explicit backpressure to measure continuous-batching + queueing interactions across mixed workloads. We want to quantify tokens/sec, p95/p99 response-time behavior, and identify configuration ranges where batching optimizations regress tail latency. This ticket covers harness additions, experiment suites, dashboards, and an initial set of runs with regression detection hooks.
acceptance_criteria: New harness can replay arrival traces with configurable inter-arrival distributions (Poisson, bursty, periodic, heavy-tailed)
Harness exposes adjustable backpressure/watermark thresholds and queue-size caps to simulate saturation and preemption
Produce standard report (CSV + Grafana dashboard) containing tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency per route, batching window metrics, queue length distribution, and KV-cache hit rates
Automated regression detection: compare new runs against baseline and flag >10% increase in p95 or >15% drop in tokens/sec
Documented experiment matrix and one example run demonstrating a batching-induced p95 regression with mixed short+long inputs
approach: Extend the async-arrival harness with an arrival watermark layer that tags requests by logical arrival time and enforces two modes: soft-watermark (admit until queue high then prioritize short sessions) and hard-watermark (reject or stall new arrivals). Instrument per-request metadata to record batch-id, time-enqueued, time-served, and KV-cache miss/hit. Use a configurable mixer to generate workload blends (ratios of short chat, long-stream generation, embeddings). Runs will sweep batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens, and queue_capacity. Baseline runs use current defaults from runtime-1.18.
experiments: Exp A: Poisson steady arrivals at 6k, 9k, 12k tokens/sec; measure throughput and p95 with batch_window_ms=20/40/80
Exp B: Bursty arrivals (50ms microbursts) with 70/30 short/long ratio; toggle soft vs hard watermark
Exp C: Mixed-session preemption: long sessions that pin KV cache interleaved with short low-token requests; measure p95 uplift on short sessions
Exp D: Regression gate: run baseline and candidate builds, compute relative p95 change and tokens/sec delta; threshold-based alerting
metrics: batch_size distribution and tail of batch formation latency
kv_cache_hit_rate and per-session cache warmup time
updates: 2026-03-03: Initial design doc posted to Confluence - link added to links field. Decided on two watermark semantics (soft/hard) after PM + Runtime sync.
2026-03-05: Prototype harness extension implemented (async-arrival fork). End-to-end single-run validated at 9k tokens/sec. Observed baseline p95 of 210ms for mixed-short workload.

2026-03-08: Discovered a skew: batch formation latency dominates p95 when max_batch_tokens set too high (>4096). Recorded a spike to p95=1.1s in a bursty scenario. Added batch_size distribution logging.
2026-03-11: Added regression gate script that compares new runs to baseline CSVs and fails if p95 increases >10% or tokens/sec decreases >15%. Hooked into CI job 'bench/regression-gate'.

2026-03-14: First comparative run between runtime-1.18 and candidate-runtime-1.19-quant branch. Candidate shows 8% higher tokens/sec but p95 for short sessions rose 22% under hard-watermark burst test. Investigating kernel scheduling changes as probable cause. Created follow-up ENG-12057 to triage kernel selection.
notes: We intentionally modelled arrival watermarks to mimic real-world traffic patterns observed from customers running mixed chat+generation workloads. Early results suggest aggressive batching/quant kernels can improve throughput but may regress tail latency for short interactive requests under backpressure. This harness will be the canonical repro for future optimizer changes. Next steps: finish experiment matrix, triage kernel scheduling, and run regression gate on nightly canaries.
